definitions: To have or retain possession of something.
To continue to have something; to retain.
To continue in a particular state or condition.
To store something in a particular place.
To maintain a record or account.
To obey or comply with (a rule, promise, or law).
examples: She decided to keep the book.
He wants to keep his options open.
The food will keep in the refrigerator.
Please keep the documents in the safe.
You need to keep accurate records.
